scope: Generic structural heuristics derived after warm-up analysis; no target-specific answers, lemma names, proof snippets or measured tactic prices. Exploratory warm-up tuning, not held-out validation.

cards.trigger: The proof reconstructs a property of an operation or representation through many small steps.
cards.action: Search definitions and nearby theorems for a characterization, composition, commutation, extensionality, or general existence theorem that directly supplies the needed property.
cards.check: Read the full signature and hypotheses; check availability in every pinned version. Avoid circular use of the target declaration.

cards.trigger: Syntax induction repeatedly extracts an invariant, typing rule, normalization fact, or relation from a separate hypothesis.
cards.action: Inspect the inductive evidence and consider induction on that evidence so its constructors provide the invariant and recursive hypotheses together.
cards.check: Verify dependent indices, generalized variables and induction hypotheses. A different induction is useful only if it simplifies the obligations.

cards.trigger: Several branches or arguments repeat the same inclusion, algebraic identity, transport, or closure reasoning.
cards.action: State one local lemma with the exact reusable parameters, prove it once, then compose it across branches or instantiate it at several values.
cards.check: Keep the helper within the proof body. Count its definition and applications in the total length; excessive generality can add elaboration work.

cards.trigger: Broad automation discovers constructors, witnesses, case facts or canonical forms that are already apparent from the argument.
cards.action: Read the constructors and supporting lemmas; supply explicit witnesses, projections and theorem applications. Leave focused arithmetic and simplification to automation.
cards.check: A slightly longer source can win on heartbeats. Do not replace every tactic blindly; check the whole declaration and version compatibility.

cards.trigger: The proof manually unfolds a finite counting, continuity, support, span, recurrence or quotient argument.
cards.action: Choose a representation that lets an existing library theorem do the central work. Search by the mathematical property and the types of the objects, not only the target theorem name.
cards.check: Prove the connection to the new representation locally, account for conversion overhead, and verify the exact assumptions.
